description: The figure presents four pie charts comparing the distribution of answer refusal categories across four language models on FACTBENCH. The 'GPT4-o' chart has two slices, with 'Lack of Knowledge' (red, 83.3%) being the larger category and 'Safety' (light orange, 16.7%) being the smaller one. The 'Gemini1.5-Pro' chart has five slices, with 'Misinformation' (orange, 38.4%) being the largest, followed by 'Lack of Knowledge' (blue, 22.1%), 'Ethical Advice' (yellow, 16.3%), 'Clarification' (light orange, 14.0%), and 'Safety' (red, 9.3%). The 'Llama3.1-70B-Instruct' chart has two slices, with 'Lack of Knowledge' (orange, 75.0%) being the larger category and 'Clarification' (red, 25.0%) being the smaller one. The 'Llama3.1-405B-Instruct' chart also has two slices, with 'Lack of Knowledge' (orange, 50.0%) and 'Misinformation' (red, 50.0%) being equally distributed. All charts have percentage labels inside the slices, and no legend is present. The slices in each chart are labeled with their corresponding categories and percentages.
caption_used: The figure presents four pie charts comparing the distribution of answer refusal categories across four language models on FACTBENCH. The 'GPT4-o' chart shows two categories, with 'Lack of Knowledge' accounting for approximately 70% and 'Safety' making up 30%. The 'Gemini1.5-Pro' chart highlights 'Misinformation' as the largest category at 45%, followed by 'Lack of Knowledge' at 20%, 'Ethical Advice' at 15%, and 'Clarification' at 10%, with 'Safety' being the smallest category at 10%. The 'Llama3.1-70B-Instruct' chart indicates 'Lack of Knowledge' as the dominant category at 80%, while 'Clarification' accounts for 20%. Finally, the 'Llama3.1-405B-Instruct' chart shows an equal distribution between 'Misinformation' and 'Lack of Knowledge,' each comprising 50%. These charts provide insights into the varying tendencies of language models to refuse answers based on different categories.
